javaVersionTooOld.title: Java version is too old for this modpack
javaVersionTooOld.explanation: One of your mods was built for a newer version of Java than the instance is currently running. Minecraft launched the game, but the mod's classes failed to load.
javaVersionTooOld.recommendation: Bump the instance's Minecraft version under Manage → Minecraft version — newer MC versions install a newer JRE automatically. If your modpack is locked to this MC version, the mod itself likely needs an update from its author.

modResolutionConflict.title: Two mods conflict with each other
modResolutionConflict.explanation: Fabric stopped loading because two of your installed mods can't run together — one requires a version of something the other forbids.
modResolutionConflict.recommendation: Open the crash log below to see which mods are named. Disable one of the two in the Installed tab and try again. If you imported a modpack, see if the pack author lists a known-bad combination.

fabricLoaderMissingMain.title: Fabric loader wasn't installed for this instance
fabricLoaderMissingMain.explanation: The launcher asked Java to start Fabric, but the Fabric loader files aren't on the classpath. This usually means the instance was created vanilla and Fabric wasn't chosen, or the loader install failed.
fabricLoaderMissingMain.recommendation: Open Manage for this instance, set the loader to Fabric, pick a loader version, and let the launcher reinstall before launching.

corruptModJar.title: A mod file is corrupt
corruptModJar.explanation: Minecraft tried to read a mod jar and found it was damaged or incomplete. The most common cause is a download that was interrupted partway.
corruptModJar.recommendation: Open the crash log below to find the jar's filename. In the Installed tab, uninstall that mod and reinstall it. If you imported a modpack, re-importing the pack will re-fetch every jar with SHA-1 verification.

outOfMemory.title: Minecraft ran out of memory
outOfMemory.explanation: The instance's allotted memory (heap) wasn't enough — typical for heavy modpacks or when many chunks are loaded.
outOfMemory.recommendation: Open Manage for this instance, raise the Max heap value (try 4096 MB for a vanilla-ish modpack, 6144 MB or more for heavy packs), then try again. Don't exceed half of your system RAM.

portAlreadyInUse.title: Network port is already taken
portAlreadyInUse.explanation: Minecraft tried to open a network port — usually for the integrated LAN server — and another program is already using it.
portAlreadyInUse.recommendation: Quit any other running Minecraft windows (including from other launchers), then try again. If the problem persists, restart the computer to clear stuck connections.

diskFull.title: Hard drive is full
diskFull.explanation: Minecraft tried to write a file (chunks, screenshots, mod cache, logs) and the disk refused because it ran out of space.
diskFull.recommendation: Free up space on the drive that holds the launcher's data — typically %APPDATA% on Windows. The launcher's Storage settings show how much space the mod cache takes if you want to start there.

serverMissingMods.title: The server needs mods you don't have
serverMissingMods.explanation: The server rejected the connection because your client is missing mods it requires, or has them at the wrong version. Minecraft listed them before disconnecting.
serverMissingMods.recommendation: Open this log and use "Install missing mods" to add them to this instance, then reconnect. Mods the launcher can't identify automatically are listed so you can find them in the Add-ons browser.

clientExtraMods.title: The server rejected some of your mods
clientExtraMods.explanation: The server refused the connection over these mods. Either the server doesn't have them, or your version differs from the server's — Minecraft can't tell the launcher which, but its disconnect screen shows any version it needs.
clientExtraMods.recommendation: Open this log. If the server doesn't have a mod, disable it (reversible) and reconnect. If it's a version difference, install the version the server needs instead of disabling.

createGoggleOverlayCrash.title: Create goggles are spamming errors
createGoggleOverlayCrash.explanation: While wearing Create goggles and looking at a mob or other entity, a Create add-on throws an error every frame. The game keeps running, but the log fills up and the goggle overlay flickers.
createGoggleOverlayCrash.recommendation: Lucerna can install a small community fix mod that resolves this. It's a third-party mod, not an official patch — review it before installing.

forgeDuplicateMods.title: Two copies of the same mod are installed
forgeDuplicateMods.explanation: The mod loader found the same mod twice in the mods folder — usually an old version left behind next to a newer one. It refuses to start until you delete one copy.
forgeDuplicateMods.recommendation: Open the Installed tab (or the mods folder) and delete the older duplicate jar, then launch again.

forgeMissingDependencies.title: A mod is missing a required dependency
forgeMissingDependencies.explanation: One of your mods needs another mod (or a newer version of it) that isn't installed. The lines after this one name the mod and the version it wants.
forgeMissingDependencies.recommendation: Install the dependency named below at the required version, or remove the mod that demands it.

fabricUnmetDependency.title: A mod's dependency is missing or the wrong version
fabricUnmetDependency.explanation: Fabric stopped loading because a mod requires something that isn't installed or is the wrong version. The lines below name exactly which mod wants what.
fabricUnmetDependency.recommendation: Install the mod named below at the version it asks for (most Fabric mods also need Fabric API), or remove the mod that requires it.

mixinApplyFailed.title: A mod failed to hook into the game
mixinApplyFailed.explanation: A mod's mixin (its way of patching game code) failed to apply. This almost always means the mod was built for a different Minecraft version, or two mods are patching the same code and collide.
mixinApplyFailed.recommendation: Check the mod named in this line. Install the build matching your exact Minecraft version and loader; if it's current, try removing it to identify the conflicting pair.

brokenModMetadata.title: A mod file has broken metadata
brokenModMetadata.explanation: The loader couldn't read a mod's descriptor (fabric.mod.json / mods.toml). The jar is malformed — usually a corrupted download or a file that isn't a mod for this loader.
brokenModMetadata.recommendation: Re-download the mod from its official page for your loader and Minecraft version, replacing the broken file.

overlayRenderCrash.title: Crash while drawing the loading overlay
overlayRenderCrash.explanation: The game died during the mod-loading screen. The 'Caused by' lines below name the mod or resource that failed to initialize.
overlayRenderCrash.recommendation: Find the mod named in the stack below and update or remove it. If a resource pack is named, disable that pack.

datapackLoadFailed.title: Datapacks blocked the world from loading
datapackLoadFailed.explanation: A datapack in this world is broken or was made for a different Minecraft version, so the world refused to load.
datapackLoadFailed.recommendation: Remove or update the offending datapack in the world's datapacks folder. Choosing 'safe mode' when Minecraft offers it disables them temporarily.

modLinkageError.title: A mod was built for a different game version
modLinkageError.explanation: Java couldn't find a method, field or class another mod expected — a mod was compiled against a different Minecraft or mod version than what's installed. NoClassDefFoundError can also be an echo of an earlier failure in the same mod — check the first error above it.
modLinkageError.recommendation: Look at the mod named in this line (or the 'Caused by' below) and install the build that matches your exact Minecraft version and the versions of the mods it interacts with.

oomMetaspace.title: Java ran out of metaspace
oomMetaspace.explanation: The class-metadata area filled up — this happens with hundreds of mods installed, independent of the normal heap setting.
oomMetaspace.recommendation: Add -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=1G to the instance's custom JVM arguments, or reduce the number of installed mods.

oomGcOverhead.title: Memory is so full Java gave up
oomGcOverhead.explanation: Java spent almost all its time garbage-collecting because the heap is nearly exhausted — effectively an out-of-memory condition.
oomGcOverhead.recommendation: Raise the instance's maximum memory (heap). For heavy modpacks try 6144 MB or more, but stay under half of your system RAM.

heapReserveFailed.title: The memory setting is larger than available RAM
heapReserveFailed.explanation: Java could not even start because the configured maximum heap is bigger than the memory the system can give it (or the value is malformed).
heapReserveFailed.recommendation: Lower the maximum memory setting, close memory-hungry programs, and make sure the game runs on 64-bit Java.

badJvmArg.title: A custom Java argument is invalid
badJvmArg.explanation: Java refused to start because one of the custom JVM arguments isn't recognized — often a typo or a flag from a different Java version.
badJvmArg.recommendation: Open the instance's Java settings and fix or remove the argument named in this line.

nativesLinkError.title: A native library failed to load
nativesLinkError.explanation: Java couldn't load a platform-native library (typically LWJGL). The files may be missing, corrupted, or blocked by antivirus.
nativesLinkError.recommendation: Run instance repair to re-download the libraries. If it recurs, add the launcher's data folder to your antivirus exclusions.

jvmNativeCrash.title: Java itself crashed (native crash)
jvmNativeCrash.explanation: The crash happened below Java, in native code — on clients this is most often a graphics-driver fault; overclocking and faulty RAM cause it too.
jvmNativeCrash.recommendation: Update your GPU driver first. If it keeps happening, remove recently added mods that use native code, and check the hs_err file mentioned nearby for the failing module.

glfwNoOpengl.title: The graphics driver doesn't provide OpenGL
glfwNoOpengl.explanation: Minecraft couldn't create an OpenGL window. The GPU driver is missing, too old, or the game ran on the wrong GPU (common on laptops with two graphics chips).
glfwNoOpengl.recommendation: Install the latest driver from NVIDIA/AMD/Intel (not just Windows Update). On dual-GPU laptops, force the discrete GPU for Java in Windows graphics settings or via the launcher's GPU option.

pixelFormatNotAccelerated.title: No hardware graphics acceleration available
pixelFormatNotAccelerated.explanation: The system offered only software rendering — the GPU driver is missing or outdated (frequent after Windows reinstalls and on remote desktops).
pixelFormatNotAccelerated.recommendation: Install the proper GPU driver from the vendor's site and restart. Remote-desktop sessions often have no acceleration — try locally.

openglErrorSpam.title: OpenGL is reporting rendering errors
openglErrorSpam.explanation: The renderer hit invalid GL state — usually a shader pack, a resource pack, or a rendering mod that doesn't match the current game or driver.
openglErrorSpam.recommendation: Disable the most recently added shader or resource pack. If it persists, update the GPU driver and rendering mods (Sodium/Iris/OptiFine) to builds for this exact Minecraft version.

invalidSession.title: The Minecraft session is invalid
invalidSession.explanation: The session token has expired or the sign-in didn't complete, so the server rejected the join. Occasionally the Minecraft session service itself is down — then waiting is the only fix.
invalidSession.recommendation: Sign out and back in (Accounts), then restart the game. On a server log this means the joining player needs to do that.

notWhitelisted.title: Not on the server's whitelist
notWhitelisted.explanation: The server runs a whitelist and this account isn't on it — nothing is broken on your side.
notWhitelisted.recommendation: Ask the server owner to whitelist your exact username (whitelist add <name>).

dnsUnknownHost.title: The server address couldn't be resolved
dnsUnknownHost.explanation: DNS lookup failed — the address has a typo, the domain is gone, or this machine has no working internet/DNS. The address is usually the server you tried to join, but mods checking for updates can log this too.
dnsUnknownHost.recommendation: Double-check the server address for typos, then verify your internet connection. If both are fine, try a different DNS (e.g. 1.1.1.1).

sslHandshakeFailed.title: Secure connection failed
sslHandshakeFailed.explanation: An HTTPS connection (login, mod download, API) couldn't be established. The most common cause is a wrong system clock; intercepting antivirus/proxy software is next.
sslHandshakeFailed.recommendation: Check that the system date and time are correct, then try again. If it persists, temporarily disable HTTPS-scanning in your antivirus or proxy to confirm the culprit.

connectionTimedOut.title: The connection timed out
connectionTimedOut.explanation: The other side never answered — the server is down, the address/port is wrong, or a firewall is dropping the traffic. (If it appears without you joining a server, a mod's background download timed out — harmless.)
connectionTimedOut.recommendation: Verify the server is running and the address and port are right, then check firewalls on both ends (including the router's port forwarding for self-hosted servers).

connectionRefused.title: The connection was refused
connectionRefused.explanation: The target machine answered but nothing is listening on that port — the server isn't running there, or it listens on a different port. (Mods' background update checks can also log this — harmless if you weren't joining a server.)
connectionRefused.recommendation: Make sure the server is running and the port matches its configuration. For self-hosted servers, confirm the port in server.properties.

sessionLock.title: The world is opened by another process
sessionLock.explanation: This world's session lock is held by another running copy of the game or server, so it can't be opened twice.
sessionLock.recommendation: Close the other Minecraft/server process that has this world open (check the system tray and Task Manager), then try again.

chunkCorruption.title: World chunk data is damaged
chunkCorruption.explanation: The game failed to read part of the world — a region or chunk file is corrupted or missing, usually after a crash or forced shutdown while saving.
chunkCorruption.recommendation: Restore this world from a backup (Worlds → Backups). Keep playing on a corrupted world only if you accept losing the damaged area.

levelDatCorrupt.title: The world's level.dat is damaged
levelDatCorrupt.explanation: The world's main metadata file couldn't be read — typically after an interrupted save.
levelDatCorrupt.recommendation: Restore the world from a backup. Minecraft also keeps level.dat_old next to level.dat — renaming it over the broken file recovers most worlds.

accessDenied.title: A file couldn't be accessed
accessDenied.explanation: The operating system blocked a file operation — the file is locked by another program (often antivirus mid-scan) or the folder's permissions are wrong.
accessDenied.recommendation: Close other programs using the folder and add the launcher's data directory to your antivirus exclusions. Avoid OneDrive-synced folders for game data.

shaderCompileFailed.title: The shader pack failed to load
shaderCompileFailed.explanation: The shader pack couldn't be compiled for this GPU/driver — it's incompatible with the current Iris/OptiFine version or the pack itself is broken. If no shader pack is installed, the rendering mod or GPU driver itself is at fault.
shaderCompileFailed.recommendation: Try a different version of the shader pack (or a different pack), and make sure Iris/OptiFine matches your Minecraft version.

serverEulaNotAccepted.title: The Minecraft EULA is not accepted
serverEulaNotAccepted.explanation: A Minecraft server refuses to start until the EULA is accepted in eula.txt.
serverEulaNotAccepted.recommendation: Accept the EULA in the server's settings (or set eula=true in eula.txt) and start it again.

serverPortInUse.title: The server port is already in use
serverPortInUse.explanation: Another program — usually another copy of this server — is already listening on the configured port.
serverPortInUse.recommendation: Stop the other process, or change this server's port in its settings and start again.

serverOutOfMemory.title: The server ran out of memory
serverOutOfMemory.explanation: The memory allotted to the server wasn't enough — common for heavy modpacks, many players, or large loaded areas.
serverOutOfMemory.recommendation: Raise the server's memory in its settings, keeping it under half of the machine's RAM, then start it again.

serverCantKeepUp.title: The server is lagging behind
serverCantKeepUp.explanation: Game ticks are taking longer than 50 ms, so game time runs slower than real time. In singleplayer the game's built-in server logs it. This is a warning about performance, not a crash.
serverCantKeepUp.recommendation: Reduce the load: fewer or lighter mods, smaller view/simulation distance, or more memory. Occasional single occurrences are harmless.

serverWatchdogStall.title: A server tick stalled — watchdog triggered
serverWatchdogStall.explanation: One tick took far longer than the configured limit, so the watchdog killed the server to break the hang. Usually one mod or one chunk operation is stuck.
serverWatchdogStall.recommendation: Check the stack printed below this line for the mod that hung. As a stopgap, raise max-tick-time in server.properties, but the real fix is finding the stuck mod.

blockingMods.title: Mods the server rejected
blockingMods.intro: The server rejected the connection over these mods. Usually your version just differs from the server's. Open the in-game disconnect screen — each mod shows your version next to the server's (the "Server has" column); install that version for the mods below. Only if a mod is genuinely missing from the server does disabling help.

welcome.title: Welcome to Lucerna
welcome.body: Lucerna organises Minecraft into instances: self-contained worlds, each with its own version, loader, mods, configs and saves, and its own isolated .minecraft directory. Switch instance and you switch your whole Minecraft install while the others stay put.
welcome.bodyBasic: Lucerna keeps your Minecraft setups in separate boxes called instances. Each box has its own game version, mods, and saved worlds. Switch to another box and everything switches with it. Your other boxes stay just as you left them.

signIn.title: Choose an account
signIn.body: You need an account to launch the game. Sign in with Microsoft, or add an offline account for single-player and LAN. Lucerna stores tokens in your OS keychain. Offline accounts can't join servers that require a Microsoft login. Reopen this menu to switch accounts, and the trash icon on a row removes one.
signIn.bodyBasic: You need an account to start the game. Sign in with Microsoft to use your real Minecraft account, or add an offline account to play on your own or with friends on the same network. Open this menu again to switch accounts; the trash icon removes one.

pickInstance.title: Pick an instance
pickInstance.body: An instance is a self-contained Minecraft install. Lucerna starts you with one called Default. This dropdown switches the active instance, so Play, mods and logs all point at whichever one you select.
pickInstance.bodyBasic: An instance is one Minecraft setup of its own. Lucerna gives you one to start, called Default. This menu picks which instance is active, so the Play button, your mods, and your logs all follow the one you choose.

manageInstances.title: Manage your instances
manageInstances.body: Manage is where you set an instance's Minecraft version and loader, tweak memory and JVM arguments, and create, rename or delete instances. A new instance starts with no version. Pick one here before you can play.
manageInstances.bodyBasic: Manage is where you choose an instance's Minecraft version and its mod system, change how much memory it uses, and create, rename, or delete instances. A brand-new instance has no version yet. Pick one here before you can play.

installPlay.title: Install, then Play
installPlay.body: The first click downloads Minecraft and your chosen loader, once per version, then verifies every asset and library against Mojang's hashes. After that the button reads Play, and Stop while the game runs. Once an instance is ready and has saved worlds, hover Play to jump straight into one.
installPlay.bodyBasic: The first click downloads Minecraft and the mod system you picked. You only wait for this once per version. After that the button turns into Play. While the game is open it turns into Stop. When your instance is ready, hover Play to jump right into a saved world.

browseMods.title: Browse mods
browseMods.body: Search Modrinth or CurseForge and install mods into the active instance's mods folder. Lucerna resolves their dependencies, SHA-verifies each file, and lists them in the Installed sub-tab.
browseMods.bodyBasic: Search Modrinth or CurseForge, two big mod websites, and add mods straight into the instance you're using. Lucerna checks each file is safe, and you'll see them in the Installed list.

importModpacks.title: Import modpacks
importModpacks.body: Drop a .mrpack or CurseForge .zip here, or browse modpacks from Modrinth, CurseForge, and FTB. CurseForge and FTB downloads need a free CurseForge API key (Settings → CurseForge). Each import lands in its own new instance and leaves your existing ones alone.
importModpacks.bodyBasic: A modpack is a ready-made bundle of mods. Drop a pack file here, or browse modpacks from Modrinth, CurseForge, and FTB. Each pack you add becomes its own new instance and leaves your other instances alone.

yourInstances.title: Your instances
yourInstances.body: Each row is one instance. Click a row to edit it, or hit "+ New instance" below to add one.
yourInstances.bodyBasic: Each row is one instance. Click a row to change it, or use "+ New instance" below to add one.

editAndSave.title: Edit and save
editAndSave.body: Name, MC version, loader, memory, and JVM args live here. Done saves and closes.
editAndSave.bodyBasic: Here you set the name, Minecraft version, mod system, memory, and some advanced options. Done saves your changes and closes this window.

openFolderDelete.title: Open folder, delete
openFolderDelete.body: Open folder jumps to the instance's directory on disk. Delete wipes the instance and all its files, after a confirmation.
openFolderDelete.bodyBasic: Open folder shows the instance's files on your computer. Delete removes the instance and everything in it, and asks you to confirm first.

verifyRepair.title: Verify and repair
verifyRepair.body: Verify checks this instance's files (client jar, libraries, assets, Java runtime, profile) against Mojang's hashes. If anything is missing or corrupt, Repair re-downloads just the bad files.
verifyRepair.bodyBasic: Verify checks that this instance's files are all present and intact. If something is missing or broken, Repair downloads just the parts that need fixing.

threeLogSources.title: Three log sources
threeLogSources.body: Game logs are Minecraft's output. Crash reports only appear when the game crashes. Launcher logs are Lucerna's own.
threeLogSources.bodyBasic: Game logs are messages from Minecraft. Crash reports show up only when the game crashes. Launcher logs are Lucerna's own messages.

displayOptions.title: Display options
displayOptions.body: Wrap lines breaks long classpath and stack-trace output. Collapse stack tucks repetitive Java frames behind a clickable row. The Show checkboxes hide whole severity levels, which helps when you're chasing a single WARN through thousands of INFO lines.
displayOptions.bodyBasic: Wrap lines keeps long lines from running off the screen. Collapse stack hides repeated technical lines behind a row you can click to open. The Show checkboxes let you hide whole groups of messages, which helps when you're hunting for one warning among thousands of lines.

searchNavigation.title: Search with navigation
searchNavigation.body: Type to search the open file. Counter shows N of M matches; Enter / Shift+Enter step through them, Esc clears. Active match is highlighted in blue.
searchNavigation.bodyBasic: Type to search the open file. It shows which match you’re on (like 3 of 12); Enter and Shift+Enter jump between matches, Esc clears the search. The current match is highlighted in blue.

shareMcloGs.title: Share to mclo.gs
shareMcloGs.body: Hover a log file in the list to reveal its actions; right-clicking a row offers the same menu. Share uploads that log to mclo.gs, the Minecraft community's de-facto paste service, and hands you a shareable link. It strips user paths, session tokens, and LAN IPs first, so you can drop the link in Discord without leaking personal info. The folder icon opens the file's folder on disk.
shareMcloGs.bodyBasic: Point at a log file in the list to see its buttons; right-clicking a file shows the same actions. Share uploads the log to mclo.gs, a website made for sharing Minecraft logs, and gives you a link. It removes your private info, like file paths and your network address, before uploading, so the link is safe to share (for example on Discord). The folder button shows the file on your computer.

crashStructuredView.title: Crash reports get a structured view
crashStructuredView.body: When you open a crash-*.txt file, Lucerna splits it into collapsible sections (Head, Affected level, System Details, Mods). Toggle Raw view in the toolbar if you'd rather grep the plain text.
crashStructuredView.bodyBasic: When you open a crash report, Lucerna splits it into sections you can open and close (like Head, Affected level, System Details, and Mods). Turn on Raw view in the toolbar if you’d rather read the plain text.

diagnosis.title: Automatic crash diagnosis
diagnosis.body: When the latest log shows a known problem, this banner names the likely cause and, for many issues, offers a one-click fix: install a missing mod, disable a conflicting one, raise the heap, and more. It always reflects the latest run, even if you open an older file in the list.
diagnosis.bodyBasic: When something goes wrong, this banner tells you the likely cause and often gives you a one-click fix. It always shows the most recent run.

readCap.title: How much log to load
readCap.body: Big logs can be slow to open, so Lucerna reads only the last slice of each file. This picks how much: bump it up to see more history, or keep it small for speed. A truncation notice tells you when a log was cut.
readCap.bodyBasic: Large logs can be slow, so Lucerna loads only the most recent part. Use this to load more or less of it.

browseVsImported.title: Browse vs Imported
browseVsImported.body: Browse searches Modrinth, CurseForge, and FTB. Imported lists packs you've already installed, each its own instance.
browseVsImported.bodyBasic: Browse searches Modrinth, CurseForge, and FTB for packs. Imported shows the packs you've already added, each its own instance.

dragAndDrop.title: Drag and drop
dragAndDrop.body: Drop a .mrpack or CurseForge .zip anywhere on this view to import. Each import lands in its own new instance and leaves your existing ones alone.
dragAndDrop.bodyBasic: Drag a pack file onto this window to add it. Each pack you add becomes its own new instance and leaves your other ones alone.

searchSortFilter.title: Search, sort, and filter
searchSortFilter.body: Search and sort are always here. Click "Filters" to pick a Minecraft version, mod loader, or source. Your choices show as removable chips, and "Clear all" resets them.
searchSortFilter.bodyBasic: Search and sort are always here. Click "Filters" to choose a Minecraft version, mod system, or website. Your choices appear as little tags you can remove, and "Clear all" resets them.

worldsWithBackups.title: Your worlds, with backups
worldsWithBackups.body: Each row is one singleplayer save, and the badge shows its backup count. Click a row to open its actions: back up now, browse past backups (restore by Replace or As-copy), or delete the world.
worldsWithBackups.bodyBasic: Each row is one single-player world, and the badge shows how many backups it has. Click a row to see what you can do: make a backup now, open past backups (and restore them, replacing the world or as a copy), or delete the world.

importWorlds.title: Import a world
importWorlds.body: Bring in a world from a .zip or a folder: drop it here, or use the folder button. Lucerna copies it into this instance's saves, so the original stays where it is.
importWorlds.bodyBasic: Add a world you have as a .zip or folder. Drop it here or use the button. It's copied into this instance, and your original file stays put.

openSavesFolder.title: Open saves folder
openSavesFolder.body: Opens the saves/ folder in your file manager so you can work by hand: move a world to another instance, or copy one out for a server upload.
openSavesFolder.bodyBasic: Opens the saves folder on your computer, so you can do things by hand: move a world to another instance, or copy it out to put on a server.

create.title: Run your own server
create.body: Spin up a Minecraft server: pick a version and loader, start fresh, or build one from an existing instance. The feature is marked Beta while it settles.
create.bodyBasic: Create your own Minecraft server here. Choose a version and a mod loader, or build one from an instance you already have.

modeSwitch.title: Two sides of the launcher
modeSwitch.body: The launcher now has two modes: Client for playing, Servers for hosting. Switch here whenever you like; the client keeps working while a server runs.
modeSwitch.bodyBasic: Use this switch to go back to playing. Your server keeps running.

startStop.title: Start, stop, and crash help
startStop.body: This sidebar button starts the server and turns into Stop while it runs; Restart sits in the panel header. If the server stops on a crash, a banner appears above the tabs with the likely cause and a one-click fix: accept the EULA, free the port, raise the heap, and more.
startStop.bodyBasic: This button starts your server, and becomes Stop once it's running. Restart is at the top of the panel. If the server crashes, a help banner appears with the likely cause and a button to fix it.

overview.title: Everything at a glance
overview.body: Overview gathers the server facts, the connection details for inviting friends, and the live console with its command input.
overview.bodyBasic: This tab shows how the server is doing, how friends can join, and what it prints while running.

addons.title: Mods, plugins and datapacks
addons.body: Add-ons adapts to the server core: mod loaders take mods, Paper and Purpur take plugins, and datapacks work everywhere. Search the catalogs or drop files onto the zone.
addons.bodyBasic: Here you add extra content. The tab only offers what your server type supports.

hosting.title: The Hosting tab
hosting.body: Hosting uploads your server to a rented host over SFTP. The first time you connect, check the host-key fingerprint to be sure you're reaching the right machine. Prefer to move it by hand? Export the whole server as a ZIP.
hosting.bodyBasic: Hosting can upload your server to a paid host over a secure connection, or export it as a ZIP file you move yourself.

toInstance.title: Make a matching client
toInstance.body: Build a client instance that matches this server, with the same version, loader and mods, so you can join your own modded server. Lucerna can add it to your multiplayer list at the same time.
toInstance.bodyBasic: This builds a matching game instance so you can join your own server, with the same version and mods set up for you. It can be added to your multiplayer list too.

kindSwitch.title: Mods, resource packs, shaders
kindSwitch.body: This row switches what you're adding: mods, resource packs, or shaders. Shaders need a shader loader to run; when you pick Shaders without one, Lucerna points you to the right loader.
kindSwitch.bodyBasic: Use this row to choose what you're adding: mods, resource packs, or shaders. Shaders also need a shader loader, and Lucerna will point you to one if it's missing.

subtabs.title: Browse and Installed
subtabs.body: Browse searches Modrinth or CurseForge for new content; Installed lists what's already in this instance. The picker on the right switches the source, and CurseForge needs a free API key (Settings → CurseForge).
subtabs.bodyBasic: Browse finds new content on Modrinth or CurseForge. Installed shows what you already have. The menu on the right switches between the two sites; CurseForge needs a free key you set in Settings.

dropzone.title: Install from a file
dropzone.body: Already have a .jar or .zip? Drop it here, or click to pick one. Lucerna checks it fits this instance's version and loader before installing.
dropzone.bodyBasic: Got a mod or pack file? Drag it here, or click to choose one. Lucerna checks it works with this instance first.

instanceConcept.body: Each instance is a self-contained world: its own Minecraft version, loader, mods, configs and saves. Switch instance and you switch your whole Minecraft install while the others stay put.
instanceConcept.bodyBasic: An instance is one Minecraft setup of its own: its own game version, mods, and saved worlds. Switch to another instance and everything switches with it, while the others stay as they were.

modpackInstance.triggerAriaLabel: Why does installing a modpack create a new instance?
modpackInstance.body: Installing a modpack always creates its own new instance: a self-contained folder with that pack's exact mods, configs and saves. Lucerna can't merge it into an existing instance, because the pack pins specific mod versions that would collide with what's already there. Isolating each pack keeps it reproducible and lets you remove it without breaking your other setups.
modpackInstance.bodyBasic: Adding a modpack always makes its own new instance: a separate setup with that pack's exact mods and worlds. It can't be mixed into an instance you already have, because the pack needs specific mod versions that would clash with what's already there. Keeping each pack on its own means it keeps working, and you can remove it without breaking your other setups.

chooser.title: How much detail would you like?
chooser.body: Show tips and the tour in plain language, or with the technical details. Change this anytime in Settings → General.

aiTranslation.label: AI translation
aiTranslation.title: AI translation
aiTranslation.aboutBody: Fill in a mod's missing translations with an AI model of your choice. Lucerna sends the English strings to the provider you pick, using an API key you supply, and keeps only the answers that pass its checks — anything it can't verify stays in English.
aiTranslation.scopeNote: This reaches the text mods ship in their own language files: item and block names, tooltips, and in-game guide books such as Patchouli. It does not reach FTB Quests, quest books, or any text a modpack keeps in its config files — that text lives outside the resource pack Lucerna writes, and stays in English.
aiTranslation.consentLabel: Let Lucerna send mod text to an AI provider
aiTranslation.consentDescription: Off by default. While it is off, no translation request leaves this computer — not even a connection test.
aiTranslation.privacyNote: The English strings from your installed mods are sent to the provider you choose and are subject to that provider's terms. A local model keeps them on this machine.
aiTranslation.modelHintCloud: Leave this empty to use the provider's default model.
aiTranslation.modelHintLocal: Required for a local model: nothing can list what your server serves, so type the name it expects.
aiTranslation.localPortHint: Lucerna only ever connects to 127.0.0.1 on this port.
aiTranslation.localNote: A small local model translates worse than a hosted one. More strings will fail Lucerna's checks and stay in English — that is the safe outcome, not a fault.
aiTranslation.keyringNote: Stored in your operating system's secure keyring. Lucerna can tell that a key is there, but never reads it back into this field.
aiTranslation.testHint: Sends one tiny request using the provider, model and key you have saved. Save a new key before testing it.
aiTranslation.testHintDisabled: Turn on the permission above first — testing the connection sends a real request to the provider.

hardcore.desc: Locks difficulty to hard and permanently bans a player on death.

pvp.label: PvP
pvp.desc: Whether players can deal damage to one another.

forceGamemode.label: Force game mode
forceGamemode.desc: Reset players to the server's default game mode every time they join.

allowFlight.label: Allow flight
allowFlight.desc: Allow flight granted by mods/plugins without kicking players for flying.

allowNether.label: Allow Nether
allowNether.desc: Enable the Nether dimension and nether portals.

generateStructures.label: Generate structures
generateStructures.desc: Generate villages, strongholds and other structures in new chunks.

playerIdleTimeout.label: Idle timeout (min)
playerIdleTimeout.desc: Kick players after this many idle minutes; 0 never kicks.

functionPermissionLevel.label: Function permission level
functionPermissionLevel.desc: Permission level required to run datapack functions and gated commands.

levelSeed.desc: Seed for world generation; empty picks a random seed.

levelType.desc: Generation preset: minecraft:normal, flat, largebiomes, amplified, or a custom id.

generatorSettings.desc: JSON customization for the world type (mainly superflat layers).

maxWorldSize.label: Max world size
maxWorldSize.desc: World border radius in blocks from the centre.

spawnProtection.desc: Radius in blocks around spawn where only ops can build; 0 disables it.

initialEnabledPacks.label: Enabled datapacks
initialEnabledPacks.desc: Comma-separated datapacks enabled when the world is created.

initialDisabledPacks.label: Disabled datapacks
initialDisabledPacks.desc: Comma-separated datapacks disabled when the world is created.

maxPlayers.label: Max players
maxPlayers.desc: Maximum number of players online at once.

whiteList.label: Whitelist
whiteList.desc: When on, only whitelisted players may join.

enforceWhitelist.label: Enforce whitelist
enforceWhitelist.desc: Kick already-online non-whitelisted players when the whitelist reloads.

onlineMode.label: Online mode
onlineMode.desc: Verify players against Microsoft/Mojang auth; turning it off allows offline accounts but lets anyone impersonate any name.

enforceSecureProfile.label: Enforce secure profile
enforceSecureProfile.desc: Require a signed chat profile; players without one can't join.

motd.label: MOTD
motd.desc: Message shown beneath the server name in the multiplayer list.

hideOnlinePlayers.label: Hide online players
hideOnlinePlayers.desc: Omit the player list from the server status shown on ping.

viewDistance.label: View distance
viewDistance.desc: Radius in chunks the server sends to each player.

simulationDistance.label: Simulation distance
simulationDistance.desc: Radius in chunks where entities and blocks are ticked around players.

entityBroadcastRangePercentage.label: Entity broadcast range
entityBroadcastRangePercentage.desc: How close entities must be to be sent to players, as a percentage of the default range.

maxTickTime.label: Max tick time (ms)
maxTickTime.desc: Watchdog crashes the server if one tick exceeds this; -1 disables the watchdog.

syncChunkWrites.label: Sync chunk writes
syncChunkWrites.desc: Write chunks to disk synchronously; safer, but can stall on slow disks.

maxChainedNeighborUpdates.label: Max chained updates
maxChainedNeighborUpdates.desc: Limit on consecutive chained block updates before extras are skipped.

networkCompressionThreshold.label: Compression threshold
networkCompressionThreshold.desc: Compress packets larger than this many bytes; -1 disables, 0 compresses everything.

pauseWhenEmptySeconds.label: Pause when empty (s)
pauseWhenEmptySeconds.desc: Pause ticking after this many seconds with no players; 0 never pauses.

serverIp.label: Bind IP
serverIp.desc: Bind to a specific network interface; leave empty to bind all.

serverPort.label: Port
serverPort.desc: TCP/UDP port the server listens on.

preventProxyConnections.label: Prevent proxy connections
preventProxyConnections.desc: Kick players whose authentication region differs from their connection (blocks some proxies/VPNs).

rateLimit.label: Rate limit
rateLimit.desc: Max packets per player per tick before a kick; 0 disables the limit.

useNativeTransport.label: Native transport
useNativeTransport.desc: Use optimized Linux packet send/receive; harmless to leave on elsewhere.

enableStatus.label: Show status
enableStatus.desc: Reply to pings so the server appears online in the multiplayer list.

acceptsTransfers.label: Accept transfers
acceptsTransfers.desc: Allow players to be transferred in from another server.

enableRcon.label: Enable RCON
enableRcon.desc: Enable the remote console for external administration.

rconPassword.label: RCON password

broadcastRconToOps.label: Broadcast RCON to ops

requireResourcePack.label: Require resource pack

enableJmxMonitoring.label: JMX monitoring

broadcastConsoleToOps.label: Broadcast console to ops
broadcastConsoleToOps.desc: Show console command output to online operators.

clientOnly.title: A client-only mod crashed the server
clientOnly.explanation: A mod meant for the game client was loaded on the dedicated server.
clientOnly.recommendation: Remove the client-only mods below, then start the server again.

portInUse.title: The server port is already in use
portInUse.explanation: Another program or server is already using this port.
portInUse.recommendation: Stop the other server, or change the port in Settings.

eula.title: The Minecraft EULA is not accepted
eula.explanation: The server won't run until the Minecraft EULA is accepted.
eula.recommendation: Recreate the server with the EULA checkbox ticked.

orphan.title: A leftover copy of this server is still running
orphan.explanation: A server process from a previous launcher session is still holding this world's files, so it can't start again.
orphan.recommendation: Stop the leftover process, then start the server.

oom.title: The server ran out of memory
oom.explanation: The memory given to the server wasn't enough — common for heavy modpacks or many loaded chunks.
oom.recommendation: Raise the server's memory below, then start it again.

heapTooBig.title: The memory setting is too large for this computer
heapTooBig.explanation: Java couldn't start because the maximum memory is bigger than the free RAM on this machine.
heapTooBig.recommendation: Lower the server's memory below, then start it again.

javaTooOld.title: Java is too old for this server
javaTooOld.explanation: A mod or the loader was built for a newer Java than the one starting this server.
javaTooOld.recommendation: Use a newer Minecraft version (which installs a newer Java), or update the mod that needs it.

corruptJar.title: A server file is corrupt
corruptJar.explanation: The server tried to read a jar and found it damaged or incomplete — usually an interrupted download.
corruptJar.recommendation: Re-download the damaged file below, then start the server again.

modConflict.title: Two mods conflict with each other
modConflict.explanation: The loader stopped because two installed mods can't run together — one requires a version another forbids.
modConflict.recommendation: Disable one of the conflicting mods below, then start the server again.

missingDep.title: A mod needs another mod you don't have
missingDep.explanation: One of the server's mods requires a dependency mod that isn't installed (or is the wrong version).
missingDep.recommendation: Install the missing dependency below, or remove the mod that needs it, then start the server again.

fabricApiMissing.title: The Fabric API mod is missing
fabricApiMissing.explanation: A mod on this server needs the Fabric API library mod, which isn't installed.
fabricApiMissing.recommendation: Install the Fabric API below, then start the server again.

mixinCrash.title: A mod crashed while starting up
mixinCrash.explanation: A mod failed during its early startup (a mixin apply error). The crash names the mod responsible.
mixinCrash.recommendation: Disable the mod named below, then start the server again.

worldCorrupt.title: The world data looks corrupted
worldCorrupt.explanation: A region or chunk file appears damaged, so the world won't load.
worldCorrupt.recommendation: Restore this world from a backup. Don't let the server overwrite it automatically — that risks losing data.

sessionLock.title: The world is still locked by another process
sessionLock.explanation: A leftover copy of this server is still holding the world's session lock, so a new copy can't open it.
sessionLock.recommendation: Stop the leftover process, then start the server again.

wrongLoader.title: A mod is for a different mod loader
wrongLoader.explanation: A file in the server's mods folder isn't a valid mod for this server's loader — usually a mod for a different loader.
wrongLoader.recommendation: Remove the mods that don't match this server's loader, then start it again.

diskLow.title: Low disk space
diskLow.explanation: The drive this server lives on is nearly full, so creating or starting it may fail or leave a half-written world.
diskLow.recommendation: Free up space on this drive, then try again.
